title: Duplicate, Delete Layer and the arrange commands in the Layers menu act on every selected row
goal: When several layers or measurements are selected, the Layers menu commands Duplicate Layer, Delete Layer, Bring to Front, Bring Forward, Send Backward and Send to Back are greyed out. They should act on the whole selection, so someone who shift-clicked three measurements can delete or restack them from the menu or its shortcuts instead of reaching for the canvas.
notes: EditorCommands.swift: the Layers CommandMenu keys every item off `selectedID` (editor?.selectedLayerID), which is nil whenever multiSelectedLayerIDs holds two or more. EditorState.deleteLayers(ids:) already batches; duplicateLayer(id:) and restack(id:) are single-layer. Add multi-aware entry points (deleteSelectedLayers, duplicateSelectedLayers, restackSelection) and enable the menu items when either store is non-empty. Same gap exists after a canvas marquee, so this also fixes the marquee case. Found while building shift/command-click list selection (audit 2026-09-02-list-multi-select rough 1). DONE: see log. Core API PhotonzDocument.restackLayers / duplicateLayers; EditorState.restackSelectedLayers / duplicateSelectedLayers / deleteSelectedLayers; menu keyed off hasLayerSelection.
acceptance: With three rows selected by shift-click, Layers > Delete Layer (command-Delete) removes all three in one undo step.
Layers > Duplicate Layer with several rows selected duplicates each one and the copies become the new selection.
The four arrange commands move the selected layers together, keeping their relative order, and stop at the locked Background.
Tests in PhotonzCore cover the reorder-with-gaps logic before implementation; Scripts/test.sh is green.

log.note: Adversarial pass before building: the menu was keyed off the single primary selection, which is nil whenever two or more rows are selected, so every batch path (shift-click, command-click, marquee) hit the same wall. Shortest fix that delivers the value: one selection-aware entry point per command in EditorState, with the batch reorder logic in PhotonzCore where it can be tested. Photoshop semantics chosen for Forward/Backward over a selection: members move one slot each, a member pressed against the top or the locked floor pins the members behind it, gaps survive.

PhotonzCore: PhotonzDocument.restackLayers(ids:_:) with RestackStep (toFront/forward/backward/toBack) and duplicateLayers(ids:offsetBy:); 14 tests in LayerBatchRestackTests written first (block moves, gaps, pinned top, locked floor, locked members ignored, single-layer parity, duplicate placement).

App: EditorState.actionableLayerIDs / hasLayerSelection, deleteSelectedLayers, duplicateSelectedLayers (copies become the selection), restackSelectedLayers (dry-run so a pinned selection costs no undo step). The Layer menu items and command-J route through them; the single-id duplicate/restack used by the row context menu act on the whole selection when the row is a member, matching how Delete already behaved. rerender now prunes a multi-selection whose layers vanished (undo of a batch duplicate), promoting a lone survivor to the primary selection.

Verified live on the probe app with a temporary harness (removed): four rectangles added, rows 2..4 selected via clickRow plain + extend, then toFront / undo / toBack at floor (unchanged) / forward / undo / duplicate (copies selected, names end in copy) / undo / delete (three gone, menu disabled) / undo restores all three in one step / selectAll marquee toBack. Scripts/test.sh green, 1270 tests. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-02-layers-menu-multi-select.json.

Layer menu Duplicate, Delete, Bring/Send commands and command-J act on the whole selection (shift-click, command-click or marquee), from the menu, shortcuts and row context menu; copies become the selection; undo prunes vanished multi-selections.
